title: 14 days to an AI engineering interview
intro: Two or three drills a sitting, 45-75 minutes. Run each one in interview mode with the timer armed before you look at the hints. Days 7 and 14 repeat drills you have already solved, which is the point: the second attempt, cold, is the one that tells you whether it stuck.

days.title: Decoding
days.focus: What temperature, top_k and top_p actually do to the distribution.

days.title: Attention
days.focus: Write it in numpy, defend the square root, then make decoding incremental.

days.title: Positions and tokens
days.focus: How a model knows where a token is, and why it cannot count letters.

days.title: Embeddings
days.focus: Pooling, normalizing, and the zero vector that turns a ranking into nan.

days.title: Chunking
days.focus: The first thing every RAG pipeline does, and the first thing it gets wrong.

days.title: Lexical search
days.focus: BM25 from the formula, over the index it actually reads.

days.title: Retrieval, timed
days.focus: Fusion and diversity, then re-run BM25 cold. No hints today.

days.title: Reliability
days.focus: React to the provider's rate limit, then stay under it.

days.title: Streaming and output
days.focus: Chunk boundaries are not frame boundaries. Parse first, repair second.

days.title: Cost and prompts
days.focus: What the bill is made of, and a renderer a user cannot inject through.

days.title: The agent loop
days.focus: A while loop with a budget, a parser, and a validator at the boundary.

days.title: Agent orchestration
days.focus: Parallelism, memory, and plans that fail without half-executing.

days.title: Evals
days.focus: Scoring, judging, aggregating preferences, and not leaking your test set.

days.title: Safety, then a mock round
days.focus: Two safety drills, then two solved ones again -- timed and cold. The real rehearsal.
